trust_decision.summary: uneval() must bound the size of the JavaScript program it emits, and that bound is decided inside its own counting/hoisting pass (src/uneval.js:152-159), not in the escaping helper: at the pinned commit the hoisting map is keyed only by non-primitive identity, so every occurrence of a long primitive string or bigint is re-emitted in full at each emission point, making output quadratic in the number of references to one shared primitive.

landing_point.why: The summary says repeated primitive strings expand quadratically, so an engineer looks at the repeated-value hoisting filter, which sorts counts and assigns IIFE parameter names; it only ever sees non-primitives because walk() counts nothing else for primitives.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A boxed `Object(x)` is an object with its own identity, so the existing identity-based hoisting looks like it already covers it, and object property keys 'cannot repeat inside one object' so key strings read as non-values.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Cheap repetitions must stay inline: uneval(['a string','a string']) is contract-tested to emit exactly '["a string","a string"]' with no IIFE, and boxed repetitions to emit exactly '(function(a){return [a,a]}(Object(1n)))'; an over-broad hoist-every-repeated-primitive fix rewrites both.

O6_input_shapes: plain string of length >= 128 repeated in an array (shared by index in the parsed wire form)
string needing escaping ('</script>\n"\\\0\u2028\u2029'), up to ~6x expansion per reference, must stay XSS-safe
distinct Object(string) / Object(bigint) boxes sharing one primitive (parse wire form ['Object', idx])
one box object repeated, which must stay one hoisted object
primitives used as Map keys and Set members, and inside sparse arrays, null-prototype objects and cyclic containers
more repeated primitives than the 65534-parameter limit, which must fall back to the array-argument form
short strings (< 128 chars) and cheap values (NaN, -0, undefined, null, booleans), which must remain inline
